'''Mansukh C. Wani''', (died 2020), was a principal scientist (emeritus) at the [[Research Triangle Institute]] in [[North Carolina]]. He was co-discoverer of [[Taxol]] and [[camptothecin]], two anti-[[cancer]] drugs considered standard in the treatment to fight ovarian, breast, lung and colon cancers. In 2000, Wani received an award for applied research in medicine, the [[Charles F. Kettering Prize]], from the [[General Motors Corporation|General Motors]] Cancer Research Foundation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-19 |title=Developmental Therapeutics Program (DTP) - NCI |url=https://dctd.cancer.gov/programs/dtp |access-date=2025-08-10 |website=dctd.cancer.gov |language=en}}</ref>

Wani was born in Nandurbar, Maharashtra, India. He attended the University of Bombay, receiving a bachelor's degree in 1947 (in chemistry) and a master's in 1950 (in organic chemistry). He moved to the United States in 1958, and received his PhD from [[Indiana University Bloomington]] in 1962, when he joined [[Research Triangle Institute]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.acsmedchem.org/?nd=Wani |publisher=ACS Division of Medicinal Chemistry |title=Mansukh C. Wani, Ph.D. |work=MEDI Hall of Fame Inductees |date=2013 |access-date=2017-07-07}}</ref> He used to live in [[Durham, North Carolina]]. He died on 11 April 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mansukh Wani, codiscoverer of Taxol, dies at age 95|url=https://cen.acs.org/people/obituaries/Mansukh-Wani-codiscoverer-Taxol-dies/98/web/2020/04|last=Wang|first=Linda|date=2020-04-21|website=Chemical & Engineering News|language=en|access-date=2020-05-16}}</ref>
